query_text: AI-assisted swarm robotics with ant colony optimization for dynamic exploration

local_candidates.title: AI-Assisted Swarm Robotics for Autonomous Exploration Using Ant Colony Algorithms
local_candidates.description: This study explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques with Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) to enhance swarm robotic exploration in dynamic and uncertain environments. While traditional ACO provides a decentralized, pheromone-based mechanism for path planning, it suffers from slow convergence, stagnation, and limited adaptability when confronted with environmental changes. To address these challenges, an AI-assisted ACO framework was developed, incorporating RL principles to adapt pheromone update rules in real time. Robots learn from past interactions, adjust strategies dynamically, and maintain efficient exploration under varying conditions. Python-based simulations were conducted across four environments—50×50, 100×100, 250×250, and 500×500 grids—with swarm sizes ranging from 20 to 200 robots and obstacle densities of 10%, 20%, and 30%. Results show that AI-assisted ACO consistently outperformed traditional ACO, achieving 7–15% higher exploration coverage (≈ 52.1% vs. 44.6% in the baseline case and ≈ 61% vs. 48% in the largest grid), with ≈ 20–25% faster convergence and ≈ 25% higher adaptability under dynamic obstacle scenarios.

local_candidates.title: RoboAuto: Autonomous Robot Program Search through Multi-Level Physical Understanding
local_candidates.description: Recently, LLM-based autonomous agents have shown strong capabilities in iteratively generating, evaluating, and refining executable solutions. In robotic manipulation, Code-as-Policy lets these agents search over modular and editable robot programs. However, effective program search requires physical understanding: agents must understand how objects can be manipulated, how scene geometry constrains actions, and why interactions succeed or fail. Existing methods rely mainly on execution feedback for program refinement, often leaving these physical questions unresolved. We introduce RoboAuto, a framework for robot program search that explicitly organizes physical understanding at the object, scene, and interaction levels through three components. First, a hierarchical knowledge base combines executable skills with object-centric knowledge of affordances, spatial relations, and action effects, learned from embodied data and online task solving. Second, scene grounding connects this knowledge to the current environment by identifying relevant objects and resolving action-critical quantities. Third, multi-stage planning with self-designed experiments checks whether each stage produces its expected physical effects and actively tests competing hypotheses to resolve physical uncertainties. RoboAuto achieves superior performance across five benchmark families, attaining an 89.1% success rate on short-horizon LIBERO-PRO tasks and more than twice the mean success rate of ASPIRE on LIBERO-PRO Long and LIBERO-Plus. It also outperforms ASPIRE and $π_{0.5}$ on three challenging long-horizon real-robot tasks requiring precise manipulation. We further show that the knowledge base transfers across simulators and embodiments, and that program search performance scales with its size. Project page: https://roboauto-ai.github.io/

local_candidates.title: Revolutionizing Supply Chains
local_candidates.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing supply chain management (SCM) by addressing challenges such as demand forecasting, logistics inefficiencies, and labor shortages. This chapter explores AI's transformative role in optimizing processes, including predictive analytics for demand planning, dynamic production scheduling, and route optimization for transportation management. AI enhances decision-making, reduces costs, and promotes sustainability by minimizing waste and carbon emissions. The chapter highlights real-world case studies, offering insights into successful AI implementations while addressing barriers such as high costs, resistance to change, and ethical concerns like algorithmic bias and data privacy. Future trends emphasize AI's role in fostering resilience, enabling crisis management, and supporting collaboration among supply chain stakeholders. By integrating AI, organizations can enhance operational efficiency, achieve sustainability goals, and build competitive, resilient supply chains for dynamic global markets.
